messages:
customer_jane: hey team — running into intermittent JSON.parse failures in our client when using SSE / structured JSON mode. ~1/200 streams end with a parse error (unexpected \u0000 or EOF). Attached a tiny repro using curl below. Can you help investigate?

customer_jane: repro curl:
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat?stream=true\" \\
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  | sed -n '1,200p' > out.txt
```

customer_jane: when I run this repeatedly sometimes out.txt ends with a trailing NUL byte or a partial object like `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}}` (no closing brackets). Client fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` or `Unexpected token \u0000 in JSON at position X`.

maria_support: thanks @customer_jane — can you paste the request id and a short sample of the raw SSE frames (the `data:` lines) when it fails? also which SDK / client are you using?

customer_jane: req_id=rz-17a9f3b2. We're using our browser client (Fetch + EventSource polyfill). Here are the last SSE frames from a failed run (raw):
```
data: {\"id\":\"msg-1\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"Hello\"}}]}


data: {\"id\":\"msg-1\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\" world\"}}]

\u0000
```

eli_engineer: looks like the final frame got corrupted with a trailing NUL and missing closing bracket. Two hypotheses: 1) an upstream proxy is splitting chunk boundaries and injecting/squeezing bytes, or 2) connection got reset midstream (TLS/FIN) and a leftover buffer produced the \u0000. Do you see any connection-level resets in your client or network logs?

devon_sre: we've seen similar mismatch when auth token refresh happens midstream and the client retries on a different connection while the original connection gets a FIN from the edge. That can leave tail fragments if a reverse proxy reuses buffers. Can you check whether your client is refreshing tokens around the same time?

customer_jane: checking logs now — yes, our client refreshes tokens every 15m; the timestamp for the failing run shows a token refresh at +0.8s from stream start and then a 401 followed by a reconnect. Attaching snippet:
```
[09:42:11] FETCH stream start req=rz-17a9f3b2
[09:42:11.8] TOKEN refresh start
[09:42:12] warn: 401 received from edge for /oauth/refresh
[09:42:12.2] reconnecting eventsource (new token)
[09:42:12.3] stream ended unexpectedly (0 bytes)
```

eli_engineer: that aligns with auth-refresh overlap. Quick mitigation options:
- on client: avoid refreshing tokens mid-request (pin token for stream duration) or queue refresh until stream ends
- on server: emit an explicit end sentinel event (e.g., `data: {\"event\":\"done\"}\n\n`) so clients can recover from partial frames
- as platform workaround, we can add a small fix to the edge to zero-out trailing buffer bytes before handing off a closed connection

maria_support: @eli_engineer can you triage whether this is more likely buffer reuse at our CDN/edge or an upstream NGINX config issue? any quick flags we can flip in customer tenant to reduce occurrences?

eli_engineer: I'll check edge traces. If buffer reuse is the root cause it's in the edge C layer; if chunked_transfer_encoding or proxy_buffering is set incorrectly on a customer-proxied path we can add a header to force `Connection: close` for now. For quick customer-level workaround: set client to `stream=false` or use line-delimited JSON (NDJSON) instead of SSE structured mode. Also try `curl --no-buffer` to avoid local buffering hiding issues.

tim_oncall: scheduling a short canary to increase keepalive timeout and disable buffer reuse on one edge node for 2 hours to see if failure rate drops. I'll also enable additional logging for req_id=rz-17a9f3b2 series.

opsbot: [automated] Trace created: trace/edge/2790019000 - increased logging, canary started on edge-node-7.

customer_jane: thanks — we'll pause token refreshes while you run the canary and report back in 1 hour. One question: is there any chance gzip or chunked encoding could be transforming bytes midstream? we do see `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` on headers.

devon_sre: chunked encoding itself is fine, but some intermediate proxies do chunk coalescing and may reuse stdio buffers; gzip shouldn't add NULs. The NUL typically indicates a leftover zeroed buffer. We'll confirm with packet captures.

eli_engineer: action items:
- customer: avoid token refresh midstream (short-term)
- eng-runtime: add optional end-sentinel event for SSE structured mode (medium-term)
- eng-infra: run edge canary to disable buffer reuse and increase keepalive (now)
- support: monitor for reoccurrence and collect raw SSE frames if it happens again

maria_support: assigning internal ticket SUP-2790019 and marking high priority. We'll update this thread when the canary results are in. :thumbsup:

customer_jane: appreciated — I'll report back with results after we run 10k requests against the canary.
